1.w: Therefore, if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort provided by love, any fellowship in the Spirit, any affection or mercy,

2.w: complete my joy and be of the same mind, by having the same love, being united in spirit, and having one purpose.

3.w: Instead of being motivated by selfish ambition or vanity, each of you should, in humility, be moved to treat one another as more important than yourself.

4.w: Each of you should be concerned not only about your own interests, but about the interests of others as well.

5.w: You should have the same attitude toward one another that Christ Jesus had,

6.w: who, though he existed in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be grasped,

7.w: but emptied himself by taking on the form of a slave, by looking like other men, and by sharing in human nature.

8.w: He humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death —even death on a cross!

9.w: As a result God highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name,

10.w: so that at the name of Jesus every knee will bow —in heaven and on earth and under the earth—

11.w: and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father.

12.w: So then, my dear friends, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence but even more in my absence, continue working out your salvation with awe and reverence,

13.w: for the one bringing forth in you both the desire and the effort—for the sake of his good pleasure—is God.

14.w: Do everything without grumbling or arguing,

15.w: so that you may be blameless and pure, children of God without blemish though you live in a crooked and perverse society, in which you shine as lights in the world

16.w: by holding on to the word of life so that on the day of Christ I will have a reason to boast: that I did not run in vain nor labor in vain.

17.w: But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice together with all of you.

18.w: And in the same way you also should be glad and rejoice together with me.

19.w: Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I, too, may be encouraged by hearing news about you.

20.w: For there is no one here like him who will readily demonstrate his deep concern for you.

21.w: Others are busy with their own concerns, not those of Jesus Christ.

22.w: But you know his qualifications that like a son working with his father, he served with me in advancing the gospel.

23.w: So I hope to send him as soon as I know more about my situation,

24.w: though I am confident in the Lord that I, too, will be coming to see you soon.

25.w: But for now I have considered it necessary to send Epaphroditus to you. For he is my brother, coworker and fellow soldier, and your messenger and minister to me in my need.

26.w: Indeed, he greatly missed all of you and was distressed because you heard that he had been ill.

27.w: In fact he became so ill that he nearly died. But God showed mercy to him—and not to him only, but also to me—so that I would not have grief on top of grief.

28.w: Therefore I am all the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you can rejoice and I can be free from anxiety.

29.w: So welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor people like him,

30.w: since it was because of the work of Christ that he almost died. He risked his life so that he could make up for your inability to serve me.
